summary: @servicetitan/widget-platform-monolith preinstall downloads Bun and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's `preinstall` hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<V>/...zip`, extracts and chmod+x's the binary, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` (`execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')])`). `setup.mjs` itself is name-obfuscated with `_0x...` identifiers. `math_init.js` is a ~728 KB heavily obfuscated file (obfuscator.io shape: `// @bun @bun-cjs` header, a rotated constant array `n7gIxM=[...]`, an array-rotator `WV8StW`, and an alphabet decoder `hc1jfK9`) which is executed under the downloaded Bun runtime during `npm install`. Fetching an alternate language runtime specifically to execute a bundled opaque JS payload is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern — it lets install-time code run outside the Node interpreter, evading Node-based scanners, and gives whoever authored the payload arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine during `npm install`. The package name impersonates the `@servicetitan` scope but the shape (obfuscated preinstall + obfuscated Bun-run payload) does not match legitimate SDK behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
